title: What is the Mission of the Church
speaker: Elder Andrew Hoy
series: What is the Mission of the Church?

outline.title: Personal Background and Context
subpoints: Experience with a young, unstable church body
Disagreement with leadership on ecclesiology and mission

outline.title: Purpose of the Book Study
subpoints: Informing the congregation on the mission of the church
Grounding the church in Scripture amidst cultural debates
Challenging individuals to align with biblical truth

outline.title: Defining the Mission of the Church
subpoints: The mission is summarized in the Great Commission passages
The church is sent to witness to Jesus
The core task is proclaiming the Gospel and making disciples of all nations

outline.title: The Broader Evangelical Discussion
subpoints: The book responds to contemporary theological trends
Engaging with questions about justice, race, and culture
Orienting the church to ask the right questions before seeking answers

summary:
Elder Andrew Hoy introduces the church's book study on *What is the Mission of the Church?* by Kevin DeYoung and Michael Gilbert. He begins by sharing his personal history with a young, emerging church that emphasized 'missional communities' over corporate worship, leading to a theological disagreement regarding the nature of the church and its mission. This experience highlights the importance of grounding the church's identity in Scripture rather than cultural trends.

The sermon outlines the primary goal of the book study: to inform and shape the congregation's understanding of the church's fundamental purpose. In an era marked by intense cultural debates regarding justice, race, and politics, the book serves as a tool to ground believers in what the church is fundamentally about. By understanding the biblical definition of the church, members can more clearly and faithfully engage with these broader societal issues.

Hoy provides a clear definition of the church's mission, summarizing it as the Great Commission: the church is sent into the world to witness to Jesus by proclaiming the Gospel and making disciples of all nations. He notes that while the book's initial answer may seem wordy, the core message is that the church's unique and central calling is evangelism and discipleship. The session concludes by orienting the congregation to the broader evangelical discussion the book addresses, encouraging them to engage with the questions raised in the text as they proceed through the study.
